wasm_feasibility_study.proposed_architecture: PocketSphinx ➔ pocketsphinx.js ➔ WebAssembly in React Browser

compatibility_answers.pipeline_compatibility: INCOMPATIBLE. The full training pipeline relies on SphinxTrain and cmuclmtk C/Python scripts that require native UNIX compilation and file system access, which cannot run in-browser.
compatibility_answers.acoustic_model_loading: YES. Pre-trained acoustic models can be loaded into WASM as memory assets.
compatibility_answers.language_model_loading: YES. ARPA format (.lm) files are compatible.
compatibility_answers.pronunciation_dictionary_loading: YES. Phonetic lexicon (.dict) files are compatible.
compatibility_answers.pocketsphinx_js_api_limitations: CRITICAL BLOCKER. Standard pocketsphinx.js wrappers are built for greedy speech-to-text decoding. They do NOT expose the raw state-backtracking trellis or forced-alignment frame-level transition APIs. Without customized C-bindings exposing PocketSphinx's internal alignment APIs, word timestamps cannot be extracted.
compatibility_answers.alignment_algorithm_in_browser: INCOMPATIBLE. Collin Fair's alignment wrapper (align/main.cc) is written as a native multi-threaded command-line C++ application relying on POSIX threads and direct filesystem I/O. It cannot run in-browser without a complete rewrite of the job-queueing architecture.
compatibility_answers.licensing_implications: NONE. PocketSphinx code and standard acoustic models are under permissive BSD licenses, which are fully commercial-friendly.

wasm_feasibility_study.verdict: NOT FEASIBLE FOR DIRECT CLIENT-SIDE BROWSER ENGINES. While the memory and footprint are highly attractive, the lack of forced-alignment API exposure in pocketsphinx.js and the native POSIX architecture of align/main.cc block direct React deployment. Any implementation would require building a custom C++/WASM build toolchain.
